doc.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau and Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1957-09-01

title: Manetta as teacher and the Black and Tan band in the District
summary: Marrero praises Manetta as a professor of music who plays two trumpets at once, and recalls playing at the Black and Tan on Abbeville and Burgundy with Manetta and Udell Wilson.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah, that's right. Teaching everything. That's right. He really is a professor. Yeah. He was a professor with Mineta, oh I'm just using a bone then. That's a black and tan. Me, Mineta, and Udel. Remember Udel, you heard the other one with Udel? Wilson. He's a piano player. He died I think. Now Udel. And now he's B-Gard. And then we had this guy Montoya playing trumpet with us. That's years ago. That's the time the district was open then. Where was that black and tan? It was on Abbeyville Street, around Burgundy Street, Abbeyville and Burgundy. It was all night, you know, sang all night. That's years and years ago. I was a young man. That's why I was a real man. Well yes. I was a young man. The easy way out of the best way. The easy way the best way. And I say if you get the easy way you get the whole way.
I don't know anything about music but I've always felt that before you can really get technique,
you know, you have to get the basic ingredients first, you know, the foundations first. The technical side, yeah.
And then most of the time you develop your own technique as you go along just by watching others.

I'll tell you, you continue Mani Mani Mani Mani whatever you do, because you know he going to learn you. And he going to learn you right. Yeah, that's true. Yeah, Mani Mani Mani going to learn you, he going to learn you right. Because he knows. And nobody can't say he don't know, because they tell a story. Well he's a professor. The man played two trumpets at one time and played a first and second, you know that. He played a trombone and a trumpet. Played a first and second. I know how he'd do it. Louis Armstrong would have sang it. Louis Armstrong would have compelled him though. Oh man, he's a professor of lawyers.
